changedBeliefs: The `stmt_cache_lookup_entry` move-to-back promotion is far more expensive per firing than its two prior experiments implied, because `resqlite_cached_stmt` is 1,632 bytes — it embeds exp 106's `read_tables[64]` (512 B) and `dep_columns[64]` (1 KB) fixed arrays. One promotion copies 4,896 bytes (three full-struct copies); eviction memmoves ~50 KB. Exp 071 (MRU scan direction + SQL hash) and exp 207 (`last_lookup` fast path) both measured this function on a SINGLE repeated SQL, a shape where the hot entry is already parked at `entries[count - 1]` so the promotion branch is never reached. Their rejections therefore say nothing about the swap; it was an unmeasured cost hidden behind two 'this function is settled' results.

The swap cost is now bounded by isolated C measurement over the real struct layout (2M iterations/lane): when it fires it costs ~60-65 ns per lookup — 85.47 vs 20.97 ns (cache=8, 2 distinct SQL), 90.14 vs 18.11 (cache=8, 4), 144.28 vs 88.98 (cache=32, 2), 146.77 vs 82.38 (cache=32, 4). Single-SQL control lanes are flat (22.42 vs 22.01; 83.01 vs 79.56), independently confirming the branch is inert on the exp 071/207 shape. Replacing the swap with a per-entry `lru_seq` recency stamp plus in-place min-stamp eviction removes that work at identical LRU policy.

That mechanism is nonetheless immaterial through the public API: ~65 ns against a ~7-10 us `selectBytes()` round trip is ~0.7% of per-call wall. Two order-flipped passes of `stmt_cache_interleaved.dart` produced no same-sign candidate-faster lane, and the decisive evidence is the control lanes — with 1 distinct SQL the promotion branch is mechanically unreachable so both sides execute identical code, yet those lanes moved +24.2% / +27.5% (pass 1) and +103.2% / +42.3% (pass 2). The harness floor is orders of magnitude above the effect. This is exp 226's shape (isolated win below the end-to-end gate), NOT exp 240's (mechanism absent on the real path) — here the mechanism survives integration and is simply too small to see.

With scan order (exp 071), scan short-circuit (exp 207), and promotion cost (exp 248) all measured and all immaterial, every component of `stmt_cache_lookup_entry` has now been bounded. The function is closed: per-call cost there is dominated by the isolate round trip, and cache bookkeeping rounds to nothing against it.

Separate from performance: `reader->last_entry` and `db->writer_active_entry` hold raw pointers to cache SLOTS whose occupant a later promotion can replace. This is correct today only because a reader's acquire and dependency-read are serialized with no intervening lookup. Stable slots would make those pointers refer to a fixed entry until eviction. Latent hazard, not a live bug — but if that serialization is ever weakened, `archive/exp-248` is the already-written fix and would be justified as a correctness change.
nextSignals: Do not spend another pass on `stmt_cache_lookup_entry` — scan order, scan short-circuit, and promotion cost are all measured and all below the floor. Reopen ONLY if (a) the per-call round-trip floor drops by roughly an order of magnitude, making a ~65 ns term material, or (b) a workload appears that performs many cache lookups WITHOUT a round trip per lookup, the only shape in which this cost could aggregate.

Methodological reminder reinforced by the control lanes: when a candidate has a mechanically-unreachable configuration, measure it as an explicit control lane. Here `distinct = 1` runs identical code on both sides, so its delta is a direct read of harness noise — it moved up to +103%, which settled the verdict faster than any amount of re-running the primary lanes could have. Cheap to add, and it converts 'is this drift?' from a judgement call into an observation.

`benchmark/experiments/stmt_cache_interleaved.dart` is kept as the durable interleaved-statement gate. It is the only harness in the repo that exercises the cache promotion path at all (exp 207's `stmt_cache_hot_sql.dart` pins one SQL and cannot reach it), so any future change to cache ordering, eviction policy, or `resqlite_cached_stmt` size should run it — particularly a change that GROWS the struct, since promotion cost scales linearly with it.
